title.narrative: Support to Territorial Administrative Reform STAR 3
Support to Territorial Administrative Reform STAR 3

description.narrative: 1.1 Objectives of the intervention STAR3's overall objective is to strengthen local government effectiveness and efficiency through enhancing the supporting framework, consolidating systems, standards, and organizational capacities in place, expanding, and sustaining service delivery innovation and best practices, and institutionalizing local government accountability to women and men for enhanced participatory governance. The overall objective is supported by the following specific objectives: 1. Local government participatory governance practices are in place and functional and encourage civic engagement. 2. Municipal systems and standards are enhanced, expanded, and consolidated for improved service delivery and overall municipal performance. 3. Government institutions, responsible for decentralization and local government, are capacitated to effectively drive policy development, coordination, and monitoring.

Denna insats stöder, via en förvaltningsfond med flera bidragsgivare, implementeringen av den territoriella administrativa reformen i Albanien genom förbättring av tillhandahållande av tjänster och insyn i kommunala beslut och utgör den tredje fasen av programmet “Stöd till administrativa och territoriella reformer”. Fonden administreras och implementeras av FN:s utvecklingsprogram (“UNDP”) i Albanien, i nära samarbete med Albaniens regering. I denna tredje fas kommer projektet att anta en modulär strategi där fokus och prioritet kommer att läggas på de nyckelaktiviteter som följer av STAR2: nämligen att utvidga OSSIS-nätverket till att omfatta administrativa enheter; främja deltagarstyrning och utvidga antagande av integritetsplanering; öka statlig och lokal förvaltningskapacitet avseende standardisering och insamling av lokala data genom utbyggnad av det nationella integrerade planeringssystemet för informationssystem (”IPSIS-systemet”) på lokal nivå för att kunna planera och övervaka resultat; och genomföra samarbete med den albanska skolan för offentlig förvaltning för tillhandahållande av standardkursplaner för lokala myndigheters personal. I enlighet med dess tillämpningsområde kommer STAR3 att arbeta i partnerskap och nära samarbete med flera offentliga kontor och byråer. Inrikesministeriet kommer att utgöra den högsta nivån av partnerskap, eftersom denna institution har det övergripande mandatet och en tillsynsroll när det gäller de strategiska, operativa och övervakande ramar inom vilka de lokala myndigheterna verkar. Programmet kommer att ha ett nära samarbete med specialiserade statliga organ t.ex. Albaniens myndighet för leverans av integrerad service (“ADISA”) avseende antagande av nationella standarder och gemensamma kontor för tillhandahållande av tjänster. Andra framstående offentliga institutionspartners inkluderar Albaniens nationella myndighet för informationssamhället (“the National Agency for Information Society”), justitiedepartementet, avdelningen för allmän förvaltning och kommissionären för översyn enligt förvaltningslagen, och den nationella myndigheten för bostäder och fastighetsregistrering (“the National Cadaster Agency”). Inom projektet kommer man också att samarbeta med lokala civila organisationer för att undersöka om framsteg görs och främja en debatt om lokala förvaltningsfrågor genom ökat medborgarengagemang och för att undersöka vilken efterfrågan som finns på gräsrotsnivå på lokala åtgärder. Projektet kommer att säkerställa att de lokala organisationer som engageras representerar specifika målgrupper, särskilt kvinnor, sårbara och marginaliserade. Projektet kommer att skapa utrymme för och bjuda in lokala myndigheter och förvaltningar för att utnyttja deras kapaciteter och nätverk i syfte att ytterligare stärka dessa funktioner. Den modulära strategi som byggts upp under utformningen av programmet kommer att göra det möjligt att snabbt genomföra andra specifika aktiviteter om ytterligare resurser erhålls.

This intervention supports the implementation of the territorial administrative reform in Albania through service delivery improvement and transparency of municipal decisions, being the third phase of the Support to Administrative and Territorial Reform programme, designed as a multiple/donor trust fund, administered and implemented by UNDP Albania, in close cooperation with the Government of Albania. . In this third phase, the project will adopt a modular approach, keeping into the focus as priority interventions only the key activities to be followed from STAR2, namely, expanding the OSSIS network to administrative units, promoting participatory governance and expanding the adoption of integrity planning, increasing central and local government capacities on standardization and collection of local data through the expansion of IPSIS system at local level to plan and monitor the performance, and collaborating with Albanian School of Public Administration for the provision of standard curricula for local government staff. In accordance with its scope, STAR3 will work in partnership and close collaboration with several public offices and agencies. The Ministry of Interior will be the highest-level partnership and project counterpart, as this institution has the overall mandate and oversight role on the strategic, operational, and monitoring frameworks where local governments operate. The programme will collaborate closely with specialized state agencies (like ADISA) on adopting national standards and joint single offices for service delivery. Other prominent public institution partners include National Agency Information Society, the Commissioner on Freedom to Information and Data Protection, the Ministry of Justice, Department of Public Administration and the Commissioner for Oversight of the Law on Civil Service, and National Cadaster Agency. The project will also engage with local civil society organizations in reviewing progress and promoting debate on local governance matters, promoting civic engagement and bottom up demand for responsive local action. The project will ensure that engaged CSOs represent specific target groups, especially women, vulnerable and marginalized ones. The project will make space and invite the engagement of the Local Government Associations, making use of their capacities and networks and aiming to strengthen these capacities further. The modular approach built in the design of the programme will enable other specific activities to be triggered in case of additional resources.

sector.narrative: Decentralisation and support to subnational government

description.narrative: During its implementation the intervention went through several unexpected contextual circumstances like government policy shifts and requests from beneficiaries for adoption of new elements. Yet, it did still remain productive towards the agreed objectives. In summary the intervention supported the development of public consultation instruments, expanded municipal integrity planning, and expanded and preserved the municipal One Stop Shop (OSS) system within the possible limits. Additionally, the project conducted for the first time a municipal readiness assessment, supported the drafting of the new National Cross-Cutting Strategy for Decentralization and Local Government (NCSDLG) 2023-2030, and developed a coherent instrument for the Strategy monitoring. As per the specific outcomes, the project has achieved the following: Outcome 1: Local government participatory governance practices are in place and functional and encourage civic engagement. The STAR3 project has implemented participatory governance practices and integrity planning at the local government level, exceeding its initial targets and fostering a culture of transparency and accountability. The development of an electronic platform for public consultations, the expansion of the integrity plans and the development of an Integrity Index are notable achievements in this domain. The support for promoting participatory governance aimed to coach and support seven municipalities in the full cycle of public consultation and participation, in accordance with Law 146/2014, "On Notification and Public Consultation." Four regional workshops were organized with the participation of the other municipalities to disseminate best practices. Additionally, an electronic platform for municipal public consultations was developed with no additional costs to the project and used by the seven municipalities plus by thirteen other voluntary municipalities. Even though the electronic platform is still functional its institutionalization has not taken place as the government envisages integrating municipal public consultations into the national register (konsultimipublik.al) in the future. The project has extensively supported the integrity planning processes at the local level as well as the knowledge transfer support to the Agency for Support to Local Government (ASLG), as part of its project objectives. While the project target was to support 15 municipalities developing integrity plans, this target has been exceeded as, by the end of June 2024, the project reports 28 municipalities (23 already completed and approved their integrity plans, and 5 in the approval stage). The last municipalities have been supported as part of the knowledge transfer provided to the ASLG through hands-on and live learning processes in new municipalities. An Integrity Index was developed through broad consultations and validations and adopted by ASLG for integrity monitoring. A municipal guide on conducting Integrity Risk Assessment and drafting the Integrity Plan is developed and disseminated to all municipalities through four regional workshops. A training programme for ASLG for the adoption of local integrity plans has been implemented. Municipalities need to integrate integrity management into their strategic objectives and policies. Complementarily, ASLG requires additional support to promote the further expansion of the integrity plans and adopt effective monitoring instruments. Challenges remain, particularly in human resources management and ensuring sustained commitment from local officials. Outcome 2: Municipal systems and standards are enhanced, expanded, and consolidated for improved service delivery and overall municipal performance. Under this outcome, the project was tasked to support three main activities: 1) the One StopShop (OSS) improvement and expansion to the Administrative Units, later on 2) the undertaking of a set of readiness assessments, and 3) responding to the government request in the project Steering Committee meeting of October 2023 for piloting the re-engineering of selected municipal services in the Municipality of Tirana. OSS improvement and expansion: the OSS related activity consisted in the consolidation, improvement and institutionalization of the municipal OSS system, and its expansion to about 240 Administrative Units. This activity was implemented partially as it was heavily impacted by the government's decision to shift exclusively to online services from May 2022, which led to the suspension of several OSS related sub-activities from May 2022 onward. Despite the suspension, the government of Albania recognized the system's utility and advised continuing support for the existing OSS system in municipal central offices for the duration of the STAR3 project. However, the OSS expansion had to be canceled and so its upgrade. The project distributed IT equipment for OSS use before May 2024 under a co-financing scheme with the municipalities, but under a different setup from the one envisaged by donors. Due to government request for non-expansion to the Administrative Units, the project did not engage in supporting the installation of IT equipment in the Administrative Units. However, OSS records indicate that 12 municipalities attempted to expand the system independently, and the system operated in 33 different administrative units from May 2022 to May 2024. Currently, the system operates in only 7 administrative units across 4 municipalities. It is worth noting that if the system had been supported and institutionalized, the number of administrative units reached would have been much higher. However, the IT infrastructure provided remains with the municipalities. From July 2021 to December 2023, OSSIS warranty and maintenance services have been provided to 52 municipalities. A Help Desk was established and functional during this period to respond to municipal calls and provide ad-hoc on the job training. OSS usage statistics report over 160,000 applications processed from Nov 2018 to June 2024, with an average of 2,500 applications per month and a saving of about 1,900 hours of travel for citizens and businesses serviced at the administrative units alone. The monthly average number of applications has remained steady from year to year, starting with a low figure in the early years, 778/month (2020), 2,887/month (2021), 4,167/month (2022), 3,842/month (2023), and 3,271/month (2024). The project has made efforts to transfer the OSS Central Infrastructure to Government of Albania, but without positive results. Without such central support, the functionality of the existing OSS to date about 30 municipalities continue to use the system may stop at any time. Municipalities would revert to their old methods of service delivery, leading to significant disruptions in municipal operations. Municipal readiness assessment The Government's request for comprehensive municipal digital readiness assessments became the new project task, formally communicated to UNDP and the partners in late June 2022. The municipal and the public readiness assessments were conducted in all 61 municipalities in Albania. The exercise was a comprehensive due diligence in each municipality about the preparedness of municipalities and their citizens for digital transformation and the adoption of governance services. The Municipal Readiness Assessment was conducted along five pillars Government, Regulation, Infrastructure, Economy, and People. The assessment produced 61 reports for each Municipality, a National aggregated report, and a Road-map report, which is the final product released in June 2024. The road-map report was based on the assessment findings, and outlines practical actions for local, national and international stakeholders to engage and support the advancement of digital transformation at the local level. It is expected that the wealth of information gathered will be useful for informed decision making by the relevant government institutions in charge of digital reform as well as by the municipalities themselves and the development partners for their current and future contribution to the digital transformation domain. Piloting the re-engineering of selected municipal services This activity was triggered by a special request by the Minister for Local Government to pilot the re-engineering of selected municipal services in the Municipality of Tirana. As a follow up, the project engaged in consultations with Tirana municipality and came to an agreement to review the functionality of the municipalities General Directorate of Information Technology, Communication, Innovation and Statistics (DITCIS). The support concluded with proposed changes for improved efficiency, including standards for data management and a minimum set of indicators, along with a guide for replicating improvements in other municipalities. While the assistance was provided within time limitations, which may have impacted the depth of analysis, it was appreciated by Tirana municipal staff, who have committed to consider and follow these recommendations. Outcome 3: Central government institutions responsible for decentralization and local government are capacitated to effectively drive policy development, coordination, and monitoring. Under this outcome, the project was tasked to 1) support the drafting and finalization of the new National Cross-Cutting Strategy for Decentralization and Local Government (NCSDLG) 2023-2030, 2) develop a monitoring framework and provide coaching to the Agency for the Support of Local Governance (ASLG) staff, and 3) assess the feasibility of extending the Integrated Planning System (IPSIS) to the local level. In relation to NCSDLG, STAR3 engaged expert resources across various thematic areas like Water and Transport, Local and Rural Development, Social Services, Environment, Forests, and Greening, Delegated functions, Legal Framework, and facilitation of the strategy chapter concerning the "Local Economic and Rural Development" pillar. STAR3 actively supported also in ensuring a consultative and inclusive decision-making process involving participants from all 61 municipalities. NCSDLG monitoring and reporting support. This activity aimed to support the Ministry of Interior (MoI) and the Agency for Support to Local Government (ASLG) in establishing a system for coordinating, monitoring, and reporting on the implementation progress of the National Strategy for Decentralization and Local Governance (NCSDLG) 2023-2030. The approach involved reviving the NCSDLG technical group, developing a monitoring system, and enhancing stakeholder capacities. This collaboration was instrumental for the establishment within ASLG of a dedicated Sector for Strategy Monitoring, with trained staff and standard operating procedures in place. The activity included also the development of a comprehensive monitoring framework with standardized tools and procedures aligned with the national Integrated Planning System (IPSIS) and the creation of an analytical monitoring instrument in Excel for data collation and report generation. Substantial efforts were invested in the design of measurability of output indicators for the 179 measures outlined in the Strategy Action Plan, the development of instructions and templates for relevant contributing institutions at the central and local levels, and provision of coaching to ASLG staff throughout the development of, and in the use of, the monitoring framework. As a result of the assistance provided ASLG has by now staff equipped with sufficient know-how and instruments for conducting the first monitoring report of the new NCSDLG. However, while significant progress has been made, the full development of a comprehensive monitoring system has still a long way to go. The project has laid the foundation for building such capacities further. Continued efforts are needed to refine and improve the monitoring and reporting system for effective policy-making and accountability in decentralization reform. IPSIS adoption at the local level The adoption of IPSIS at the municipal level involved several consultations on considering IPSIS as a central monitoring instrument for public administration through the engagement of an international expert to assess the situation, options, and next steps. The final findings and recommendations suggested that IPSIS is an instrument not consolidated at central level and is premature to plan its expansion at local level as several preconditions need to be met.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
